history.summary: IDENTITY FLAG: Bharatpur's city centre holds TWO Laxman temples - an older ~400-year-old shrine in the main market said to have been established by the sage Naga Baba, and this royal temple on Laxman Mandir Road (Gur Ki Mandi/Pai Bagh) founded by Maharaja Baldev Singh and completed by his son Balwant Singh; travel writers note the two stand close together, so the CSV row may refer to either (verify which). The royal temple's legend: Baldev Singh met the saint Sant Dass, a great devotee of Laxmanji, laid the foundation, and then declared his son Balwant Singh his successor; the idols were enshrined in Vikram Samvat 1947 (1890 CE). It is built of almond-coloured Bansi Paharpur sandstone with white marble on the first storey, with ornate relief work - floral patterns and birds on the jagmohan front, ceiling, doors, pillars, walls and arches - and smaller idols of Hanuman, Shatrughan, Bharat and Ram. The Bharatpur royal family regards this and the Deeg Laxmanji temple as their royal temples (per a pujari account on velpu). name: Laxman Temple
town: Bharatpur (Laxman Mandir Road, Gur Ki Mandi/Pai Bagh)
town_description: Bharatpur is a city in eastern Rajasthan, former capital of the Jat kingdom, known for the Lohagarh Fort and the Keoladeo National Park. The Laxman Mandir stands on Laxman Mandir Road in the Gur Ki Mandi/Pai Bagh area of the city centre, close to the main market where a second, older Laxman shrine also stands.

travel.road: Central city on Laxman Mandir Road; no parking at the temple - walk or take an e-rickshaw/auto (per visitor reviews)
